tasks.title: Resume a single release candidate without replacing shipped assets
tasks.acceptance: Persist candidate/source/release SHA/version/digests. Resume after main-pushed/tag-missing and upload interruption from the same candidate. Build once and reuse artifacts; existing assets must match digest, otherwise stop rather than clobber. Verify externally retrievable GitHub assets.
tasks.last_evidence: commit 4e44473, released as v0.24.5. The repair step's `gh release upload "$tag" dist/* --clobber` replaced a published asset without comparing it: measured with a stub `gh` and a real `dist/`, a release already carrying a wheel with digest sha256:aaaa... let the step exit 0 after logging `UPLOAD upload v9.9.9 dist/*.whl dist/*.tar.gz --clobber`, so an interrupted-then-rebuilt upload would publish a build no run chose. The step now reads `gh release view --json assets` (gh 2.97.0 does report `digest`) and compares each published sha256 against `sha256sum` of the file this run built: absent names upload, matching digests are left alone and named, a different digest stops the run with both digests plus the `gh release delete-asset` repair, and a missing digest also stops it. Only the artefacts that are already right are skipped, so a half-finished upload still finishes. tests/test_release_recovery.py grew six tests over real files and a stub that now answers `--json assets`; 6/6 mutations caught. 4279 passed in 178.52s, 251 formatted, demo unchanged (5 claims - 4 verified, 0 moved, 1 missing, worst high, exit 1); CI Test 43662926891 success, Auto release 43663238464 success. Not tried: no real interrupted upload on a hosted runner; the evidence is the step body executed against stub state. Reproducibility half (commits eeb4e09 and 123db56, released as v0.24.6): two builds of one tree produced different digests (wheel dce5bd60... vs 52eaddf2..., sdist 8f7f7b56... vs 16ca8704...) while every extracted member was byte-equal - the clock lives in zip member times, in sdist member mtimes and in the sdist's gzip header, which is not a member at all. New tools/normalise_artifacts.py rewrites both archives to one epoch (SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH, else the HEAD commit time, else 0) and release.yml runs it between the build and the wheel smoke test, so the digest that is published is the digest of the wheel that was installed; measured identical after the change (wheel 2230171c..., sdist 681131a1...). tests/test_reproducible_build.py builds twice and compares, reads the gzip header's own mtime (a same-second comparison cannot see it) and requires the digest to move with the epoch. That suite first shipped red on all 11 CI jobs for two reasons unrelated to reproducibility: the dev extra never promised `build` (clean checkouts died with `No module named build` while lint and sdist hid it by installing build by hand), and the epoch tests asked the checkout for a commit time, which is true in a clone and false in an unpacked sdist. Both repaired in 123db56: dev now names build>=1.0 and setuptools>=77, the five epoch tests stub the two clock sources rather than interrogating the directory, and tests/test_extras.py gained the guard that would have caught the first hole (every module the suite -m-runs must be promised by the extra). 4291 passed in 190.98s, 253 formatted, demo unchanged (5 claims - 4 verified, 0 moved, 1 missing, worst high, exit 1); CI Test 43667078866 was the red run, Auto release on 123db56 succeeded and published v0.24.6. 5/5 mutations caught plus a comment-only control that must and does survive.; commit f0b756f, released as v0.25.0. The release page named files and gave digests but nothing tied those bytes to a commit, so a resumed release could only assume its rebuild was the same build - which is why the v0.24.5 digest guard could refuse a different build without ever defining what the same build was. New tools/release_candidate.py writes dist/release-candidate.json before the smoke test: version, tag, candidate/source/release commits, and sha256+size for every file in dist except itself (a file cannot carry its own digest). release.yml writes it after normalising the artefacts, and a new final step downloads what the release actually serves (gh release download) and runs check on that directory - the only place in the pipeline where the published thing is read instead of written. First production evidence, taken tonight against the real API: `gh release download v0.25.0` then `python tools/release_candidate.py check` prints `matches its record: version 0.25.0, 2 artefact(s), release b53380fe319da027cd0ba3da3112aa184113ddab`, exit 0, with candidate f0b756fdcef1751e6fa90a7cfaa989c34ec3e58f. tests/test_release_candidate_record.py 24 tests; 9/9 mutations caught plus a comment-only control that survived; 4315 passed in 190.83s; 255 formatted; demo 4 verified/1 missing/high/exit 1; Test 43672194153 success, Auto release 43672506274 success; https://github.com/lyear12/citevouch/releases/tag/v0.25.0; commit 7982c12, released as v0.26.0. The last acceptance clause: a resumed release rebuilt its artefacts and hoped the bytes matched what the tag already served, which stopped being safe once the v0.24.5 digest guard began refusing to replace a differing asset - an honest re-run then had to produce byte-identical output, which a changed toolchain makes false. New `reuse` subcommand of tools/release_candidate.py compares the record's identity (version, tag, and the tested commit when the caller knows it) before handing over to `check`, because a record from another release passes every digest comparison and is still the wrong release. A new step before `Build` runs `gh release download`, sets `reusable=true` only when that command exits 0, and `Build` plus the record step are skipped together so a downloaded directory keeps the attribution of the run that built it. A failed download is the first-release path rather than an error, and every doubt rebuilds. tests/test_release_reuse.py exercises the command, the workflow wiring, and the step body itself against a `gh` stub in three states (no release / recorded bytes / drifted bytes); tests/test_release_candidate_record.py split its 'neither new step is conditional' assertion into 'the retrieval check is never conditional' and 'the record is written only when these bytes were built'. 4334 passed in 195.38s, 256 formatted, demo unchanged (5 claims - 4 verified, 0 moved, 1 missing, worst high, exit 1); mutations caught=7/7 with a comment-only control held. CI Test 43676081014 success and Auto release 43676416883 success published v0.26.0; fetching it back gives `matches its record: version 0.26.0, 2 artefact(s), release 66b3cdbb...`, exit 0, candidate 7982c1218b476565b9e1a1d2910fb9f1966d47a0. Not tried: no production run has yet taken the reusable=true path, because every release so far was the first for its tag.

tasks.title: Correct automation and metrics claims
tasks.acceptance: Document implemented CI/release/smoke behavior separately from missing issue consumer, review, merge and retrospective executors. Keep original failure categories. Do not infer no users or product success from zero issues/download counts; distinguish bot and independent evidence.
tasks.last_evidence: commit 5c1f22b, released as v0.26.1. Three documents described machinery nobody had run. docs/maintenance.md drew a loop in which the nightly reads the day's commits and promotes recurring lessons; nightly.yml has five steps that find the newest release by version, install its wheel in a clean venv, replay init-demo plus verify, and file or update a nightly-dogfood issue on failure - no step reads a commit - while LESSONS.md carried `reviewed-through: none` and an opening sentence saying 'Each night the day's commits are reviewed'. The same page listed issue consumption, review and merging as loop stages: nothing consumes an issue, `gh api repos/lyear12/citevouch` reports main unprotected with rules [] and PR list [], and there is no merge bot. docs/metrics.md, whose stated purpose is repeatable measurement, documented `gh api repos/.../releases`: measured 2026-11-15 that call returned 30 releases / 83 downloads, ?per_page=100 returned 100 / 306, and --paginate with per_page=100 returned 255 releases / 732 downloads, so the file taught a command that silently measured a slice. Rewrites: the loop diagram marks every stage automated or not and ends with the retrospective marked not built; a new 'What is automated, and what is not' table names the four unautomated stages and their cost; the retrospective section is titled '(not yet automated)' and states the marker reads none; LESSONS.md's opening paragraph now says the retrospective does not run yet. metrics.md documents per_page=100 plus --paginate, prints both the truncated and the real totals, replaces its counts paragraph with a signal/what-it-can-support/what-it-cannot table (the nightly downloads the newest wheel daily, this session fetches releases too, so an even dusting across all releases is automation while a person arrives at one release), states 'zero issues is not evidence that nobody uses it, and it is certainly not evidence that it works', and gives the zero-downloads trigger a third column saying a tool nobody can install cannot demonstrate need either way and that the measurement cannot tell those apart. nightly.yml was read but not changed: its steps already match the description once the description was corrected, and changing a working job to match a document would have been the wrong direction. tests/test_automation_claims.py (10 tests) parses nightly.yml and holds the documents to it. Reverse validation: 13 of 13 restored wordings turn the tests red and a comment-only control stays green; the first two passes of that script caught 6 and then 11 of 12 because the tests asserted that a noun appeared instead of that the denying sentence existed. 4344 passed in 198.51s, 257 formatted, demo unchanged (5 claims - 4 verified, 0 moved, 1 missing, worst high, exit 1); CI Test 43679398052 success, Auto release 43679761561 success, https://github.com/lyear12/citevouch/releases/tag/v0.26.1. Not tried: the nightly job itself was not executed - the assertions read its step names - and the metrics numbers were measured today against the live API and will age. PyPI still returns 404, so the funnel caveat remains open and CV-010 is still the owner action.
